request.state: The Can dev workflow should let a coding agent follow one link from a syntax error to the correct v1 construct. Existing owners are split: normative grammar syntax, design semantics, compiler-position completion, a finite UI design catalog, and a builtin function catalog. Availability must distinguish source syntax, checked compiler support and chosen local runtime resources; an approved proposal is not automatically a working suggestion. A reviewable pre-plan deliverable is needed now, with one signature, meaning, example, availability and stable link per eligible construct. Compare equivalent approaches for one authoritative agent-help surface and low ongoing drift.

help_ownership.instructions: Select the best source arrangement for durable, context-eligible Can help cards, considering present effort and future dev-server use.

criteria.dynamic_completion: Build help at request time from live parser/completion plus references. It follows current syntax directly, but lacks durable authored meanings/examples and may produce unstable links or IDs.
criteria.compiler_registry: Maintain a versioned structured registry next to compiler completion with authored card fields and profile availability, using explicit consistency checks with source owners. Machine-readable immediately, though some metadata repeats the docs.
criteria.documentation_registry: Publish one anchored Markdown table of cards and statuses first and defer machine extraction. Easy to inspect and link today, but shipping code later needs careful conversion and synchronization.
criteria.derived_sources: Attach card fields to the grammar and component/builtin owners and generate a merged index with profile support. Canonical fields remain near their owners, at the price of a multi-source generator and delivery metadata join.
